name: Head of the Dragon
prompt:
A card picture for a 1990s-style fantasy trading card game, hand-made traditional media with visible texture, the matte, slightly faded look of a printed 1990s card. One clear subject that fills the frame, its focal point near the centre, readable at a glance even very small. Keep the bottom-left and bottom-right corners dark and simple. Landscape 3:2. No text, no letters, no inscriptions, no border, no frame, no logo, no watermark, no signature. Not photorealistic, not 3D render, not modern digital concept art, not anime, not a glossy oil painting.

Setting: the War in Heaven from the Bible (Genesis, 1 Enoch, Isaiah, Revelation): fallen angels, giants, demons and the beasts of the Apocalypse, shown as Christian sacred art showed them.

Look: a hand-coloured woodcut from an early printed Bible of the 1500s. Heavy black carved lines and dense parallel hatching cut into wood, coloured afterwards by hand with bright, transparent washes that slip outside the lines: sky blue, red lead, yellow, green and violet, on rough off-white rag paper with grain and foxing. Vigorous, slightly crude and dramatic, like the Apocalypse and Creation prints of the Reformation Bibles. Make it climactic and terrifying, a scene of awe and dread: towering scale, violent diagonal motion, deep black hatched shadows against blazing light, the figure looming over the viewer.

Subject: One head of the great red dragon of Revelation 12, with seven heads and ten horns, whose tail swept a third of the stars from heaven: a crowned horned dragon head roaring, coils and falling stars behind it.
